subject: Biology
objectiveMappingPolicy: Official objectives are retained at topic level because the cited KIE syllabuses do not map each objective one-to-one to a numbered sub-topic.

source.title: Secondary Education Syllabus Volume Two

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: distinguish between continuous and discontinuous variations

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: describe the structure and properties of chromosomes

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: state the first law of inheritance and describe Mendel‟s work

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: construct and use punnet square/checker board

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: distinguish between F1 and F2 generations, genotype and phenotype, haploidy and diploidy, homozygosity and heterozygosity, dominance and recessiveness, linkage and sex linkage, mutations and mutagens

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: predict and explain the inheritance of the ABO blood groups and Rhesus (Rh) factor

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: state examples of genetically inherited disorders

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: explain causes of chromosomal mutations

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: explain the practical application of genetics.

subTopics.name: Linkage Sex linked genes, sex linked characteristics e.g. Colour blindness, Haemophilia, Hairy ears and Nose

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: explain the meaning of evolution and the current concepts of evolution

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: describe the struggle for existence and survival for the fittest

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: describe the evidences for organic evolution

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: explain resistance to antibiotics, fungicides and pesticides.92

topics.name: RECEPTION, RESPONSE AND COORDINATION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: define irritability, stimulus and response

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: explain differences between tactic and tropic responses and their survival values

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: explain the production of plant hormones and their effects on tropisms (growth responses)

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: relate the structure of the mammalian nervous system to its functions

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: distinguish between simple and conditioned reflex actions

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: explain the role of endocrine system in humans

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: state the effects of drug abuse on the human health

objectives.label: h)
objectives.text: relate structure to function of the human ear and eye

objectives.label: i)
objectives.text: explain defects of the eye and ear and their corrections.

subTopics.name: Meaning of stimulus, response and irritability
Reception, response and coordination in plants
Reception, responses and coordination in animals
The role of hormones in coordination in a mammal
Effects of drug abuse on the human health
Structure and functions of parts of the mammalian eye (human)
Structure and functions of parts of the mammalian ear (human)

topics.name: SUPPORT AND MOVEMENT IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

objectives.label: a)
objectives.text: explain the necessity of support and movement in animals and plants

objectives.label: b)
objectives.text: describe the arrangement and the role of supporting tissues in young and old plants

objectives.label: c)
objectives.text: list functions of the exo and endoskeletons

objectives.label: d)
objectives.text: describe locomotion in a named finned fish

objectives.label: e)
objectives.text: identify the bones of the axial and appendicular skeleton in a mammal

objectives.label: f)
objectives.text: describe the structure and functions of different types of joints in a mammal and explain how muscles bring about movement

objectives.label: g)
objectives.text: distinguish between the different types of muscles, their locations and functions.

subTopics.name: Identification of the bones of axial and appendicular skeletons (names of individual bones of coccyx not required)
Types and functions of movable joints (ball and socket, hinge joint)
Structure, function and location of cardiac, smooth and skeletal muscles (Details of fine structure not required) Role of muscles in movement of the arm in humans
